Concrete case plus a workaround.

I run subagent-heavy sessions. On one session the built-in sidebar showed $1.21 spent while its 81 child sessions had spent $6.41 on top of that, so roughly 84% of the real cost was invisible. That matches the reconciliation posted above.

Instead of waiting for the core fix I wrote a TUI plugin that walks the child tree with `client.session.children` and renders the rollup below Context (additive with it, not inclusive): https://github.com/JLegends/opencode-subagent-usage

Two notes for whoever implements the real fix:

- The plugin API has no children accessor on `api.state.session`, so a plugin has to go through the SDK client. A first-class accessor would help.
- `session.cost` moved between reads while I was testing, so a rollup derived at read time will age better than a snapshot taken once.

Still want the core change (#47822, #48548) — this is a workaround, not a substitute.

Same root cause, with two extra data points that might help narrow it.

I hit this writing a sidebar plugin, and saw two failure modes that appear to depend on whether the package ships its own copies of `solid-js` / `@opentui/*`.

**Package with no local copies** (only optional peers declared, none installed): the plugin does not run at all. A top-level side effect in the module never fires and the plugin never appears in the plugins dialog. The only variable I could isolate was JSX:

- `.tsx` with TypeScript syntax only, no JSX, in the installed package referenced through `exports["./tui"]` → loads, top-level marker written.
- the same file with `<box>`/`<text>` added → never executes, no marker, no error, plugin absent from the dialog.

**Package with its own copies**: matches #48883, it loads, may paint once, then never updates because the signals belong to a second Solid runtime.

Workaround that works today, verified end to end from an npm install: ship precompiled plain JS rather than TSX. `jsx`/`jsxs` from `@opentui/solid/jsx-runtime`, getters on every prop that reads reactive state, and no local copies of `solid-js` / `@opentui/*`. That renders and updates live. Two packages doing this now: https://github.com/JLegends/opencode-subagent-usage and `@pistonex/opencode-go-usage` 0.1.3 from #48883.

One request: please pair this with #41574. None of these paths emits a diagnostic at any log level, so a broken plugin and an unloaded plugin look identical from the outside. A single "plugin X failed: unresolved jsx runtime" line would turn a multi-hour hunt into a one-minute fix.

> Yourkaikai nailed the mechanism: Continue and Retry keep replaying the same poisoned context, so the thread can never dig itself out and only a fresh session works. That exact loop is what pushed me to write a workaround instead of waiting. It is a single-file Python script with no dependencies that opens the local opencode database and strips out just the stale caller-bound reasoning material, leaving messages, tool history and file edits exactly as they were. Afterwards the bricked session opens again, minus only the hidden reasoning the server would not accept anyway. https://gist.github.com/goainwo0/5df39ec984904d082d77e3e4da4a5a6e [@yanhenrique-dev](https://github.com/yanhenrique-dev) [@Yourkaikai](https://github.com/Yourkaikai) tagging you both since you hit it head-on. Two practical notes. First, Yourkaikai, on your macOS point: the script asks opencode itself where the database lives and then checks the usual locations on all three OSes, so the platform difference should not matter. Second, shut opencode down before running it, the database file is locked while the app runs. I validated it against a copy of a large database, confirmed the poisoned rows were gone and plain history stayed intact, and a second run reports everything already clean. Unofficial, and the upstream recovery PRs are still pending, but it restored sessions that looked permanently dead.

Thank you very much, this will be of great help.

> [@GooseOb](https://github.com/GooseOb) I found a deterministic config-dependent trigger for this error.
> 
> Environment:
> 
> * OpenCode official release: 1.18.31
> * Linux
> * OpenCode Zen free tier
> * Official OpenCode CLI
> * Valid `ses_...` session IDs
> 
> Baseline works:
> 
> OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1 \
> opencode run --pure \
>   -m opencode/big-pickle \
>   "Reply with exactly: ZEN_OK"
> 
> Result:
> 
> ZEN_OK
> 
> The issue appears when certain tool permissions are denied.
> 
> Minimal reproduction:
> 
> {
>   "provider": {
>     "opencode": {}
>   },
>   "default_agent": "probe",
>   "agent": {
>     "probe": {
>       "mode": "primary",
>       "model": "opencode/big-pickle"
>     }
>   },
>   "permission": {
>     "glob": "deny"
>   }
> }
> 
> This produces:
> 
> Error: Error from provider (Console): OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode
> 
> Changing only:
> 
> "glob": "allow"
> 
> makes it work again.
> 
> The same happens with:
> 
> "grep": "deny"
> 
> → same 403.
> 
> But:
> 
> "list": "deny"
> 
> works normally.
> 
> I also tested a larger permission configuration. Changing only:
> 
> - "glob": "deny",
> - "grep": "deny",
> + "glob": "allow",
> + "grep": "allow",
> 
> while leaving the rest of the permissions unchanged made the free-tier request work again.
> 
> So in my testing:
> 
> glob: "deny" → 403
> grep: "deny" → 403
> glob: "allow" + grep: "allow" → works
> list: "deny" → works
> 
> This looks like a reproducible interaction between the free-tier request path and the available tool set / tool permissions.
> 
> I am not claiming this is the underlying root cause, but it is a consistent trigger and workaround on my setup and may help narrow down the issue.

Can confirm that the workaround can make things return to normal.

Another data point for this from the provider side. We run an OpenAI-compatible inference gateway; a user reported "garbage output" that turned out to be this rendering path rather than the model or the wire.

**Variant: flat lists, tail blanked rather than overdrawn.**

The answer contained a flat bulleted list and a flat numbered list, no nesting. Every list item rendered with only its first few characters and the rest of the line was *blank* — not spliced with text from another item. Surrounding paragraphs rendered perfectly.

| sent | drawn by the TUI |
|---|---|
| `- Built an offline replica ... ` (~250 chars) | `- Built` |
| `- Parser: 0 errors; analyzer: 14 warnings; smoke test: all 5 pass` | `- Parser:` |
| `1. Re-copy <path> to your scripts folder (replace the old one)` | `1. Re` |
| `2. Verify: <three name/value pairs in backticks>` | `2. Verify` |
| `3. Re-run: <command> - it should now ...` | `3. Re` |

**The cut points are SSE chunk boundaries, not character positions.** `- Parser:` kept its colon while `2. Verify` lost its colon. Upstream those arrived in differently batched deltas — `" Parser"`+`":"` together in one chunk, `" Verify"` and `":"` in two. No character-count, width, or word-break rule produces both of those; "whatever arrived in the item's first delta survives" produces exactly both.

**This corroborates your clipboard finding from the other end of the wire.** We confirmed server-side that the bytes left us whole:

- the assembled response body we archive is the full, intact text;
- we replayed that same answer through our streaming relay in 801 deltas, deliberately split mid-word and across list markers — 2002 chars in, 2002 chars out, byte-identical.

So the text is complete when it leaves the server, and per your investigation it is also complete in `opencode.db`. Only the screen is wrong, which fits the cursor-repositioning / line-height explanation you landed on.

**Caveat, stated plainly:** I have *not* reproduced this locally. It is a production observation reconstructed from the rendered output plus the server-side record, on the released TUI against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (GLM 5.3, streaming, `Build` agent). I don't have the reporter's exact version; 1.18.31 is what we have locally. So please treat the flat-list case as a second symptom worth checking against whatever fixes the nested-list cursor offset, rather than as a standalone repro.

If it would help, I can try to produce a minimal repro against a local mock SSE endpoint that emits a flat list token-by-token.

Reproduces deterministically in my environment (opencode 1.18.31, npm install on Linux/Arch, Ghostty; logged into OpenCode Zen + OpenCode Go).

**Repro:** start a fresh session whose active agent is a custom primary agent (named `review`) while the active model is `opencode/big-pickle` (Console). The first request fails immediately, every time:

`Error from provider (Console): OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`

In the *same* session, switching to `build` or `plan` streams with the identical model without error (35 successful `opencode/big-pickle` streams in that one session within minutes).

**Log excerpt (UTC):**

failures (every attempt):

```
01:34:41.402 stream providerID=opencode modelID=big-pickle agent=review mode=primary
01:34:41.735 stream error AI_APICallError: Error from provider (Console): OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode
01:35:31.505 stream providerID=opencode modelID=big-pickle agent=review mode=primary
01:35:32.143 stream error ... free tier can only be used from within OpenCode
01:42:38.644 stream providerID=opencode modelID=big-pickle agent=review mode=primary
01:42:39.472 stream error ... free tier can only be used from within OpenCode
01:45:38.321 stream providerID=opencode modelID=big-pickle agent=review mode=primary
01:45:38.892 stream error ... free tier can only be used from within OpenCode
```

same session, working:

```
01:36:05.967 stream providerID=opencode modelID=big-pickle agent=build mode=primary
01:36:09.086 stream providerID=opencode modelID=big-pickle agent=build mode=primary
...
```

**Observations**
- Gate is free-tier-specific here: `review` with a Go/paid model (`opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`) never fails (0 errors in the same window); free-tier Console models fail.
- It is not strictly agent-specific in the broader logs: the same gate has intermittently tripped on other free-tier Console models under `build`, `plan`, and `title` as well. But for `opencode/big-pickle` it fails on the *first request* of every new session in the `review` agent while `build`/`plan` in the same session immediately succeed — which points at the free-tier client/session marker check (MissingSessionID-type) rather than the agent itself.

Note: the issue body reports version 1.3.17 (pacman); the 1.18.31 npm build reproduces it 4/4 in this session.
